name: Orbit AI - Internal Team Messaging - Tag for Action (05 Section 14, new - not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Tag for Action webhook
nodes.notes: 05 Section 14: '@username (or @AI-employee) + action + company (autocomplete), OR Opportunity ID paste + @target + note. Human-to-human: personal notification + action button, logs to Activity Event. Human-to-AI: same mechanism - read-only/reversible = immediate response, external-send/billing/irreversible = same human-approval gate regardless of trigger.' Called by Command Center's handlePostTagForAction (src/messaging/routes.ts) - the compose form on /messaging is the actual UI, this workflow is where the CRM write and AI-employee gating logic live, same 'every CRM write goes through n8n' architecture as everything else in this repo. Input contract: {targetType: 'human' | 'ai', targetIdentifier: string (an email/handle, or the literal 'ai-employee'), action: string, opportunityId: string | null, note: string, taggedByEmail: string}.

nodes.name: Log Activity Event

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ type: 'TagForAction', opportunityId: $json.body.opportunityId, targetType: $json.body.targetType, targetIdentifier: $json.body.targetIdentifier, action: $json.body.action, note: $json.body.note, taggedByEmail: $json.body.taggedByEmail, at: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Logs to Activity Event' per spec, verbatim - the durable record, whether the target is human or AI. Same Activity Event timeline dnc-check.workflow.json's override log and W4.4's AI Activity Summary both write to. opportunityId can be null (a Tag-for-Action doesn't strictly require one, per the spec's 'OR Opportunity ID paste' framing implying it's not always present) - Twenty CRM's own handling of a null foreign key on this write is unconfirmed, same REST-shape uncertainty as everywhere else.

nodes.name: Notify human target

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ recipientEmail: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.targetIdentifier, summary: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.taggedByEmail + ' tagged you: ' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.action + ' - ' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.note, linkUrl: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId ? (($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/opportunity/' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId) : null }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Personal notification + action button' per spec - the notification IS the delivery, the 'action button' is the linkUrl-based deep link Command Center renders (same pattern Step 3 already built for alerts). Reuses the Command Center Alerts Ingest credential (ALERTS_INGEST_SECRET) - Command Center's own routes.ts treats /api/notifications as the same trust boundary as /api/alerts, not a second secret.

nodes.name: Call Claude

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-opus-5', max_tokens: 1024, system: [{ type: 'text', text: 'You are the AI employee for a sales team CRM. A rep tagged you with a reversible, read-only request (summarize/research/draft only - you never send anything externally from this path). Respond concisely and directly with the requested output, no preamble.', cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } }], messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Action: ' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.action + '\nNote/context: ' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.note }] }) }}

nodes.notes: A real call, same credential/header pattern as post-call-synthesis.workflow.json (W3.4) - plain text response, not Structured Outputs, since a summarize/research/draft request doesn't have a fixed schema the way a call disposition does. cache_control on the static system instructions per the brief's prompt-caching-required rule.

nodes.name: Extract Claude response
nodes.notes: Same unwrap-the-response-envelope pattern as post-call-synthesis.workflow.json's own extraction node - throws (routing to errorWorkflow) rather than silently passing through nothing if the text block is missing.

nodes.name: Log AI response Activity Event

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ type: 'AiActivityResponse', opportunityId: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId, respondingTo: 'TagForAction', responseText: $json.aiResponseText, at: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: The AI's own response gets logged to the same Activity Event timeline as the original tag - a rep reading the Opportunity's history sees the request AND the answer, not just one half. This is also the record 05 Section 10's 'AI Activity Summary' automation (W4.4) would read from.

nodes.name: Notify tagger: AI responded

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ recipientEmail: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.taggedByEmail, summary: 'AI employee responded to your "' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.action + '" request: ' + $('Extract Claude response').item.json.aiResponseText.slice(0, 200), linkUrl: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId ? (($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/opportunity/' + $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId) : null }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Read-only/reversible = immediate response' - the rep who tagged the AI sees the answer show up as a personal notification right away, not by having to go check the Opportunity's Activity Event timeline themselves. Truncated to 200 chars in the notification summary - the full response lives in the Activity Event logged above, this is just the alert.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, delivered: 'ai-response', response: $('Extract Claude response').item.json.aiResponseText }) }}

nodes.name: Create AI action request

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ action: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.action, note: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.note, requestedByEmail: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.taggedByEmail, opportunityId: $('Tag for Action webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId }) }}

nodes.notes: 'External-send/billing/irreversible = same human-approval gate regardless of trigger' - per spec, verbatim. Deliberately does NOT call Claude at all on this path: nothing executes until a human approves it on Command Center's /messaging page (handleResolveAiAction) - approving there is a UI action only, per this pass's scope; actually EXECUTING an approved gated action (e.g. really sending the drafted email) isn't built - that needs its own resume-after-approval mechanism this repo doesn't have yet, flagged rather than faked.
